# Chapter 9: Common Design Patterns — 9.2.4–9.2.10

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 9.2.4 Making an Async Variant of an Existing Synchronous Method

- **FDG9033** DO keep parameters in the same order in the synchronous and asynchronous variants of a method, when possible. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9033
- **FDG9034** DO convert the signature as needed to remove any `ref` or `out` parameters from an asynchronous method. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9034
- **FDG9035** CONSIDER replacing synchronous callbacks with asynchronous callbacks in the Async method, or accepting both via overloading. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9035

## 9.2.5 Implementation Guidelines for Async Pattern Consistency

- **FDG9036** DO NOT return a null `Task` or `Task<TResult>`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9036

## 9.2.5.1 Task.Status Consistency

- **FDG9037** DO NOT return tasks in the `Created` state. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9037
- **FDG9038** DO throw an `OperationCanceledException` when aborting work due to a `CancellationToken`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9038

## 9.2.5.2 Awaiting on the Correct Context

- **FDG9039** DO use `await task.ConfigureAwait(false)` when awaiting an Async operation, except in application models that depend on the synchronization context. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9039

## 9.2.5.3 Avoiding Deadlock

- **FDG9040** DO NOT invoke `Task.Wait()` or read the `Task.Result` property in an Async method; instead, use `await`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9040
- **FDG9041** DO call asynchronous method variants, instead of synchronous method variants, in the implementation of Async methods. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9041

## 9.2.5.4 Properly Handling ValueTask and ValueTask&lt;TResult>

- **FDG9042** DO NOT operate on an instance of `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` more than once or save it; only ever `await` or `return` it. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9042

## 9.2.5.5 Exceptions from Async Methods

- **FDG9043** DO throw usage error exceptions directly from the Async method, to aid in debuggability. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9043
- **FDG9044** DO throw execution error exceptions via the Task-like value returned from an Async method. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9044

## 9.2.10 IAsyncEnumerable&lt;T>

- **FDG9045** DO use the suffix “Async” for methods returning `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9045
- **FDG9046** DO add the `[EnumeratorCancellation]` attribute to the `CancellationToken` parameter of an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` method using `yield return`. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9046
- **FDG9047** DO NOT use `IAsyncEnumerator<T>`, or any other type that implements or extends that interface, except as the return type of a `GetAsyncEnumerator` method. (partly checked) (not in test projects)

## 9.2.6.5 Usage Guidelines for await foreach

- **FDG9049** DO use the `WithCancellation` modifier when using `await foreach` on an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` parameter for the purpose of using your `CancellationToken` with the enumerator. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9049
- **FDG9050** DO use the `ConfigureAwait` modifier when using `await foreach` in the same way that you would with `await`. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-async-consistency.md#fdg9050
